reasoning_notes: Ranked by: (1) strict causal order—events must follow chain sequence temporally; (2) chain coverage—complete chains (5-6 events) score highest, partial chains (3-4 events) score moderate; (3) independent sourcing—averaged 2.0+ sources per event indicates multi-site reporting; (4) geographic spread—5+ distinct regions/8+ sites signals cross-organizational signal vs. local routine traffic; (5) contradiction count—zero contradictions favor genuine emerging risks. GENUINE subset (14 candidates, 'real'): Tier 1 complete chains with strong multi-region independent reporting: C-12 & C-30 (cert_rotation→revenue_miss, 5/5 events, 3.8 avg sources, 4-6 regions), C-28 (full supply chain 6/6, 3.3 sources, 6 regions), C-39 & C-47 (attrition_spike→account_churn, 5/5 events, 3.2-4.0 sources, 6 regions). Tier 1b complete 4-event chains: C-6 (policy chain 5/5), C-34 & C-45 (policy chain 4/5, missing audit), C-59 (attrition 4/5, missing backlog). Tier 2 pricing chains: C-53 & C-56 (4/4 complete price_increase→forecast_revision, consistent 2.8 sources, 5 regions). Tier 2 strong 3-4 event chains: C-7 (attrition 4/5), C-9 (policy 4/5, 5.5 avg sources), C-38 (supply defect→escalation, 6.0 sources). ARTIFACTS (lowest tier): Events out of temporal order (C-5, C-11, C-16, C-24, C-32, C-37, C-54); single-site/source routine traffic (C-35: all events 1 source, 3 regions); scattered events across multiple unrelated chains (C-20). Discriminative features: causal order violation is strongest artifact indicator; single-site concentration despite multiple events; average independent sources <2 per event (local reporting); geographic spread <3 regions.
